question_answers.question: identity/scope
question_answers.answer: The BTS Gold Line G3 terminus in front of Taksin Hospital — a 2020 people-mover stop, not an MRT stop, and not the ICONSIAM stop (that is G2, ~500 m away); catchment 83.9% Khlong San district plus a Samphanthawong sliver over the river.

question_answers.question: everyday experience
question_answers.answer: A residential west-bank district stitched to a mega-mall riverfront: temples and low-rise sois inland, ICONSIAM's River Park and decks ~500 m away, commute via a one-stop people-mover hop to the BTS.

question_answers.question: values+mechanisms
question_answers.answer: High transport and vibe scores ride on the Gold Line-to-BTS hop and the riverfront's gravity; food 9 leans on the mall and district sois; the west-bank address buys river proximity at below-riverside rents.

question_answers.question: counter-evidence
question_answers.answer: Green 5 (0.2 ha) is genuinely low; nightlife 9 against 10 venues looks edge-dependent; Gold Line ridership is small and falling through 2026.

question_answers.question: rhythm
question_answers.answer: Morning and evening commute pulses through G3 and Krung Thon Buri; mall evenings and weekend riverfront crowds; residential quiet otherwise; everything winds down by midnight with the line.

question_answers.question: walkability
question_answers.answer: Flat west-bank grid with the station at Taksin Hospital's door and Somdet Chao Phraya Road frontage; no walking durations derived from catchment radius in this bundle.

question_answers.question: daily life
question_answers.answer: Daily needs run through district sois (65 essentials POIs per app) plus the mall; 11 temples and riverside heritage shape the backdrop; piers give river access.

question_answers.question: affordability vs stated figures
question_answers.answer: App 19,000/42,500 sits below PropertyScout's luxury-skewed listing means (1-bed ~27-28k) — consistent with non-riverside stock and budget pockets (7-10k reported in Khlong Ton Sai); the 2-bed 42,500 is far under the riverside-skewed mean, implying a mid-market blend.

question_answers.question: green/quiet with polygon honesty
question_answers.answer: The unit's own green is a 0.2-ha remnant; the district's named parks and ICONSIAM's River Park sit outside or at the edge — green 5 is honest, quiet is real inland of the riverfront.

question_answers.question: conditional fit
question_answers.answer: Strong fit for renters who want a residential address with riverfront weekends and a one-hop BTS commute; weak fit for park users, late-night dwellers, or anyone requiring frequent rapid transit (a 2.77M/year people mover).

question_answers.question: recent changes 2024-2026
question_answers.answer: Free-fare week (Jan 2025), earthquake suspension (Mar 2025), declining 2026 ridership, ICONSIAM ICS/hotel addition (2023) — but no confirmed Phase 2 or new rail infrastructure in body-read sources.

question_answers.question: uncertainties/outside-the-score
question_answers.answer: Unresolved: identity of the 0.2-ha park object, which two piers the app counts, ICONSIAM's edge-membership in this unit, the fare's 15-vs-16 discrepancy, and peak train frequency (summary-only); anchors verified clean.

editorial.preview: A west-bank residential district with a 2020 people-mover stop, one hop from the BTS, facing the city's most ambitious riverfront mall across 500 metres of Charoen Nakhon Road.
editorial.guide_lead: Khlong San station ends the BTS Gold Line on Somdet Chao Phraya Road, deep in a low-rise, temple-dotted west-bank district — with ICONSIAM's riverfront a short hop down the line at Charoen Nakhon station and the BTS Silom Line one stop beyond that.

strengths.text: A rare combination for the price band: residential west-bank quiet with a direct people-mover link to the BTS Silom Line and river piers for cross-river life.
ICONSIAM's retail and river park sit just off the unit's edge, giving mall-grade daily life without a mall-grade address premium.

tradeoffs.text: Public green is nearly absent inside the unit (0.2 ha) — the big parks named for the district sit beyond the catchment and the riverside park is private.
The Gold Line is a light people-mover: ~2.8 million riders a year system-wide, service to midnight, and a 2026 ridership slide — not a trunk line.

day_night.text: Days run on school, hospital and commuting traffic with mall weekends; after dark the action stays at the riverfront edge while the sois empty early — the line itself stops around midnight.

within_area_variation.text: The river-facing corner near the Charoen Nakhon station edge carries the mall's energy and the 16.1% Samphanthawong share; the streets around Taksin Hospital and the district office are the quiet, village-like core.

conditional_fit.text: Choose it if you want mid-market rents (app 19,000 for a 1-bed) with riverfront weekends and a one-stop BTS commute — families and quiet-preferring renters fit best.
Skip it if you need parks at the door, late-night streets, or heavy rapid-transit capacity — green is 0.2 ha and the people mover is small.

uncertainties.text: Unresolved: which 0.2-ha object the app counts as park; which two piers; whether ICONSIAM falls inside this unit's polygon edge (~500 m by coordinates); fare 15 vs 16 THB; peak frequency is summary-only; anchors verified against OSM with no mismatch.
